references.text: Moses' father-in-law Jethro gave advice on appointing leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens—the same organizational structure described in Deuteronomy 1:15.
The Lord commands Moses to gather seventy of Israel's elders to help carry the people's burden, a parallel to the appointment of leaders.
The list of tribal heads who were to assist Moses with the census shows the same principle of selected leaders from the tribes.
The command to appoint judges and overseers (שֹׁטְרִים) in all the cities, the same office mentioned in Deut 1:15.
Joshua commands the overseers (שֹׁטְרִים) to go through the camp, continuing the same leadership structure after Moses.
Bezalel is filled with wisdom (חָכְמָה) from God, the same quality that the selected leaders were to have according to Moses.
The apostles ask the congregation to choose seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and wisdom—matching the criteria for wise and well-known men in Deut 1:15.
